<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1f0b3419ff818c5b97c2d0c00dc917410a67e8b2`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1f0b3419ff818c5b97c2d0c00dc917410a67e8b2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b513eabdc4b92f077956a4f127a73e2682265505` — the merge of head `0155b343ef2c723a5a92f6c1a52b3a67b1db69cd` into base `1f0b3419ff818c5b97c2d0c00dc917410a67e8b2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b513eabdc4b92f077956a4f127a73e2682265505 && git checkout b513eabdc4b92f077956a4f127a73e2682265505
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1f0b3419ff818c5b97c2d0c00dc917410a67e8b2 0155b343ef2c723a5a92f6c1a52b3a67b1db69cd && git checkout -B drift-repro 1f0b3419ff818c5b97c2d0c00dc917410a67e8b2 && git merge --no-ff 0155b343ef2c723a5a92f6c1a52b3a67b1db69cd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1f0b3419ff818c5b97c2d0c00dc917410a67e8b2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1f0b3419ff818c5b97c2d0c00dc917410a67e8b2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0155b343ef2c723a5a92f6c1a52b3a67b1db69cd`

<sub>Reviewed and posted 2026-09-23T16:55Z by the at-tier review subagent the `domain:spec#5` seat spawned — inputs: card #19846 and its 3 comments, #15705 (9 comments), #19900, PR #19899 (merge-base diff `dabf8d795e..0155b343ef`, 12 files, 7 commits, 46 check-runs), AGENTS.md, contract-review.md, execution-duties.md; objectui read at the pin `62597c5880`. Read: the whole diff and every producer named below. Ran: the three screen suites, the two runtime pin files and the spec pin at head in a detached worktree; four ablations (three re-measured from the dev's set, one my own) and one edge probe on the real engine. NOT MEASURED: the map-strip ablation (A3), the dev's claim that boundary construction 1 is unreachable through a shipped door, and the derived gate family (read from CI, per the rule).</sub>

### ① Derived judgments

**Producers of an `AutomationContext` that start or resume a run** (my census: every `.execute(` into an automation engine/service over `packages`, `examples`, `apps`, non-test, plus the engine's trigger `start` callback at `engine.ts:3607`; the service registered as `automation` is the engine itself, `plugin.ts:617`, and `resolveRunContext` spreads `...context`, `engine.ts:5038`, so the key reaches `screen-nodes.ts:236` unfiltered):

| producer | signal | judged |
|---|---|---|
| trigger door `domains/automation.ts:1305` via `buildAutomationContext` — `POST /:name/trigger`, legacy `POST /trigger/:name` | filled | right; both routes pinned, 12/12 measured |
| declarative `type:'flow'` endpoint `endpoint-executor.ts:537`, same builder | filled | right; `callerParamKeys: ['reason']` pin measured |
| action door `action-execution.ts:947` `dispatchFlowAction` — REST `/actions` (`domains/actions.ts:753`, `params: reqParams` = raw `body.params`) and MCP `run_action` (`domains/mcp.ts:727` → `invokeBusinessAction:2261`, `params` = raw `input.params`) | filled | right; nothing is merged into the caller's bag upstream on either path (the `{...reqParams, recordId, objectName}` merge at `actions.ts:741` is the script/sandbox branch) |
| schedule (`schedule-trigger.ts:806`), time-relative (`:726`), record-change (`:499`), api/webhook (`api-trigger.ts:143`) — through `engine.ts:3607` | absent → inference | right per the ruling's scope; schedule's non-record seeds are #19900 |
| `subflow-node.ts:114`, `map-node.ts:193` child runs | stripped → inference | right: these are the only two `engine.execute` sites in `builtin/`; `parallel`/`loop`/`try_catch` run regions of the same run against the same bag, so the parent's list is the right list there |
| `examples/app-showcase/src/security/seed-approval-demo.ts:308` direct `engine.execute` | absent | right |
| `engine.resume` (`run.context`, `engine.ts:6783`), `retryExecution` (same context), `bubbleToParent` (parent's own persisted context) | not a start | no foreign list is possible: `ResumeSignal` (`automation-service.ts:503`) carries no context; both stores JSON-clone on save and load (`suspended-run-store.ts:145,178,183`), and a `string[]` survives — the durable pin went red under A1 |

Can a caller make a filled list name a key it did not supply, or omit one it did? No and yes-by-design: both lists are `Object.keys` of the caller's own bag minus the door's row-id keys, nothing else; the omission is the row-id set only.

**Row-id keys.** Trigger door leaves out `recordId` and the object-id alias: right against shipped clients — objectui `useConsoleActionRuntime.flowHandler` at the pin mirrors the row id into `params.recordId` (line 578) before posting to that door; `RecordDetailView.flowHandler`, the SDK `automation.trigger` and verify's `flows.run` (`handle.ts:369`) reach the same door. Action door additionally leaves out the action's `recordIdParam`: on `main`, `flows.mdx` already says the id seeded "under an action's declared `recordIdParam`" is not "the caller supplying a screen value" (diff context lines 44-46), while the inference honoured that only by value. **Measured edge (my probe on the real engine, required field named like `recordIdParam`, caller value ≠ row id):** no signal → run continues with the caller's value; door-shaped signal → paused. Not an accept-set narrowing: no request key is refused, the value still lands in the bag (`{...seeded, ...params}`), no authorable key or export is removed — `execution-duties.md:65` asks whether the accept set widens or the public surface grows; AGENTS.md's `(narrowing)` arm is for a removal or rename an author can write. Plain `Clause-②: yes` is the right arm; no ADR-0087 disposition owed. The changeset states the edge (its last bullet).

**Pins.** Head: service-automation 41/41 (11 new + 24 + 6 untouched), runtime 62/62, spec 2/2. Ablations (each mutated file hash-checked, restored with `checkout HEAD --`, blob == HEAD, tree clean): A1 signal read removed → 6 red of 41, BOUNDARY 1 and BOUNDARY 2 both red plus the durable-store pin; A2 subflow strip removed → 2 red of 11; A6 trigger-door exclusion removed → 5 red of 12; my own action-door exclusion removed → 3 red of 12.

**Sentences that ship.** Docblock, changeset, `flows.mdx`, PR body: the door list, the absent-producer list and the strip list equal my census; the inference paragraph in `flows.mdx` matches the four legs of `callerSupplied` at head; the replaced "known gap" paragraph was false since `4177ed3a84` (value comparison, #16392) as claimed; "no security middleware keys on it" — the twelve files naming the key are the PR's own; "one existing pin edited" — the diff's only modified test is `endpoint-executor.test.ts`. No false sentence found. Two incompletions, not falsehoods: `flows.mdx` names the trigger door without the legacy route the docblock and changeset name; the changeset's "two constructions still skipped" is the engine-level verdict (the dev's own report says construction 1 is not producible through a shipped door — NOT MEASURED by me).

**Dev-report claim that is misattributed (not in shipped text):** the action door's `recordIdParam` exclusion is justified by objectui `resolveRecordIdParamSeed`, but at the pin that call sits in the console's **api** handler (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:415-426`; `RecordDetailView.tsx:685` names it the apiHandler mirror), which never reaches `dispatchFlowAction`; console flow actions use the trigger door. The exclusion stands on the published `flows.mdx` sentence, not on that client.

Governed surfaces: none in the file list. Model identifiers: swept the diff, all seven commit messages and the PR body for every spelling — none.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec` **minor** — a new optional member on the published `AutomationContext` (`./contracts` export): correct, and it is what makes `Clause-②: yes` true.
- `@objectstack/runtime` **minor** — no new entry-point export (`buildAutomationContext`/`dispatchFlowAction` are not on `index.ts`); the doors emit a new signal: at least right.
- `@objectstack/service-automation` **patch** — `HeadlessScreenContext` is new but `screen-input-contract.ts` is not re-exported by the package entry (exports map is `.` only), so no public surface moves; the behaviour is a skip→pause fix: defensible (minor would also be).
- Arm: plain `yes`, consistent with the changeset (no `(narrowing)`; nothing removed). `Check Changeset` success.

CI at the head, 46 runs de-duplicated by name keeping the latest `started_at`: 35 checks, 31 success, 4 skipped by design, 0 red — `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` (latest run is the seat's body-edit `edited` event, excluded by `pr-automation.yml`'s `github.event.action != 'edited'`; their earlier push-event runs succeeded), `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` (label `needs:pack-smoke` absent), `Console Pin Gate` (`needs.filter.outputs.console` false: no console path touched). All seven required contexts success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 (webhook trigger absent):** answered — A. The ruling names the action and trigger doors; `api-trigger.ts:143` seeds `params` as a copy of the payload it also sets as the record, so today's inference pauses; filling from the payload would move webhook screen behaviour without a ruling.
- **Q2 (`recordIdParam` left out; arm):** answered — keep, plain `yes`, no ADR-0087 disposition (① above, with the measured edge).
- **Key name `callerParamKeys`:** accepted — camelCase TS config key, reads as what it is.
- **Locally unmeasured (dev):** full spec suite and the out-of-package importers of `AutomationContext` — covered by `Test Core` (6/6 shards) and `Type Check · workspace`, both success.
- **#19900 (schedule seeds answer a screen):** correctly filed as class a, `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by: #19846`; the only trigger with non-record seeds, so the class ends there.

Blocking: none.
Non-blocking: (1) the dev report's `resolveRecordIdParamSeed` justification is misattributed (api handler, not the flow door) — the shipped text does not carry it; (2) `flows.mdx` omits the legacy trigger route from its door list; (3) service-automation could equally be `minor`; (4) A3 and the boundary-1 reachability claim were not re-measured here.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19846-automation-caller-provenance`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1` — at-tier review subagent spawned by the `domain:spec#5` seat

**VERDICT: PASS**
